proposals.evidence: DEDR4711(a) explicitly gives Toda mēṇ ‘tree’, oblique mēṇt-. Survey mēn matches this Toda branch, retaining its plain nasal notation rather than using subsection(b)’s animal compounds. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR5264 explicitly gives Alu Kurumba bari thatched roof, Irula bärī roof and Toda pary roof of hut. The corresponding barɨ/barī/pəri survey forms fit these language-specific reflexes; differing vowel notation is preserved, including the census source’s uncertain Toda label. The questioned Kurukh ridge-beam comparison is not used. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4616 explicitly gives Tamil makaṉ and Malayalam makan/mōn son, Kannada maga/makan, Tulu mage and Toda mox child/son. The selected southern survey makan/magan/maga/mahan-type responses preserve the family, including k/g/h variation and nasalized or nasal-cluster lect forms. These minority-lect assignments are comparative proposals; ambiguous contractions and longer compounds are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4004 gives Tamil/Malayalam paḻam ripe fruit, Irula pammu/pāmu, Toda pum, Kannada paṇṇu, Parji pal, Gondi paṇḍ(i) and Konda paṇḍu. Selected survey paḷam/payam/pagam/paśam/pām- responses preserve lect-specific reflexes or loss of the medial retroflex, and Kannada/related annu reflects loss of initial h-. These are comparative family proposals; the separate Indo-Aryan-looking phal forms and opaque responses are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
